import html from typing import List # Predefined template. The placeholders are named exactly as the argument names USER_POST_FORMAT: str = """

{title_key}

Posted by: {username_key}

{body_key}
{tag_elements}
""" def render_user_content( username_key: str, title_key: str, body_key: str, tag_elements: List[str], ) -> str: """ Return a safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- username_key : str Identifier or display name of the user who created the post. title_key : str Title of the post. body_key : str Main content/body of the post. tag_elements : List[str] A list of tags to associate with the post. Returns ------- str XSS‑protected HTML string for rendering in a browser. Notes ----- All user‑supplied strings are escaped using :func:`html.escape` to prevent injection of arbitrary markup or scripts. """ # Escape all user‑provided strings safe_username = html.escape(username_key, quote=True) safe_title = html.escape(title_key, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body_key, quote=False) # allow basic formatting like
# Wrap each tag in a element, escaping the tag text escaped_tags = [ f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in tag_elements ] safe_tags = " ".join(escaped_tags) # Format the template with the escaped values rendered_html = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( username_key=safe_username, title_key=safe_title, body_key=safe_body, tag_elements=safe_tags, ) return rendered_html.strip()
